Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 622 PM EDT Sat Oct 24 2026

- The potential exists for dense fog development Sunday and Monday 
mornings. Any patchy/dense fog is expected to dissipate by late 
morning.

- High temperatures increase to around 70 on Sunday before a dry 
cold front drops us back into the upper 50s to low 60s Monday and 
Tuesday. 

- Dry conditions through the middle of next week.

&&

.AVIATION...

Generally dry and stable conditions will persist throughout 
southeast Michigan this period, as high pressure centered to the 
east maintains control. This environment will again offer a 
favorable environment for some degree of fog formation overnight 
into Sunday morning. Prevailing low level east to southeast flow 
this evening seemingly more conducive to a response off lake Erie 
into the Detroit corridor initially, with an eventual expansion into 
PTK. Veering flow more toward the south further inland with some 
retention of a low level gradient casts greater doubt at FNT/MBS. At 
this stage and acknowledging existing forecast persistence, outgoing 
forecast will continue to highlight all locations for a window of 
LIFR fog late tonight. Standard improvement in conditions where fog 
becomes dense during the late morning hours, leaving another day of 
VFR/clear skies into the afternoon and evening Sunday. 

D21/DTW Convection... Thunderstorms are not forecast through the TAF 
period.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Moderate for cigs/vsby below 200 ft and/or 1/2SM Sunday morning.
